parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the large sklearn-pandas project scope, including mapper behavior, feature generation, numerical transforms, pipeline integration, package metadata, documentation, and tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It used swarm mode and divided ownership by file family: DataFrameMapper, pipeline, features/transformers/cross_validation, packaging/API, docs, and root tests, then later delegated a repair pass to agent-6.
parallel.implementation: The first six children produced project files and local scratch checks, but the integrated root pytest run still exposed 7 failures across complex object handling, transformed_names behavior, and gen_features expectations.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent inspected the shared /workspace tree and imports, then attempted an integration repair by launching agent-6; that repair result was never completed or joined before the artifact was finalized by timeout.
parallel.verification: The parent ran an import sanity check and `python -m pytest test.py -q`, observing 7 failed and 18 passed tests before starting the repair child.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Agent-6 had pending alignment tasks for pipeline, dataframe_mapper, features_generator, cross_validation, __init__, tests, and final pytest, but was cancelled; official evaluation later failed 65/70.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same sklearn-pandas package, source, test, docs, packaging, compatibility, and verification obligations from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main agent owned the entire pipeline, downloading/copying upstream v2.2.0 sources and tests, then making local adaptations without inter-agent handoffs.
serial.implementation: It copied the upstream package and tests into /workspace, adjusted __init__.py and setup.py for the required API and dependencies, added spec-interface tests, and patched README doctest output for the installed environment.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All source, tests, docs, and metadata were integrated in one workspace and the final structure included both required files and an upstream tests directory.
serial.verification: It ran upstream tests, spec cases, full pytest including README doctests, setup.py checks, root test.py, and final import checks; final verification reported 70 passed plus all spec tests passing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved implementation or verification work remained in the observed trajectory; the session completed normally and official evaluation passed 70/70.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel captured the same high-level package requirements and child prompts included detailed expected behaviors for each file family.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial captured the whole prompt directly and used upstream source and test references to satisfy the package, docs, packaging, and compatibility requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly comparable; the meaningful difference was not missing top-level requirements but the parallel run failing to complete the later repair needed to satisfy them.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated six distinct implementation/documentation/test ownership slices, then a seventh alignment repair child after integration failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept ownership centralized in the main agent, so source copying, adaptation, testing, and closure stayed in one local sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit owners for the main work but added a late critical repair owner whose output never returned; serial avoided that handoff boundary by keeping repair in the main flow.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The initial child briefs included detailed file scopes, and the repair prompt supplied concrete failure details and upstream-reference goals to agent-6.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial consumed upstream source and tests directly and kept the discovered environment/test adjustments in the same context window.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no supported context-loss label: agent-6 received actionable context, but the handoff became unusable because the active repair turn was interrupted before producing results.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel initially assembled generated modules and tests, then discovered concrete behavioral mismatches and planned alignment to the real v2.2.0 implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial copied the upstream implementation and tests first, then applied targeted API/dependency and README doctest adaptations until tests passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial used a reference-first path that reached a validated implementation, while parallel's repair path was started only after an already-failing assembled implementation and did not complete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The six initial child results returned, but the later repair child was active with required tasks pending when it was interrupted and returned as failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; the main agent completed its final step and prompt normally after verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The decisive lifecycle difference is that parallel's needed repair result was stopped before it could be finalized or joined, while serial's local result reached normal completion.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel agents wrote into the shared workspace by assigned file ownership, and the parent performed an import/tree check before discovering integrated test failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated source, tests, docs, and metadata in a single workspace and kept the final artifact tree coherent, including upstream tests and data.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete concurrent overwrite or artifact leakage is proven; the integration difference is that parallel left unresolved cross-file behavior after a cancelled repair, whereas serial reconciled and retested the final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran root pytest and saw 7 failures; official completed evaluation later recorded 65 passed, 5 failed, and solution_passed false.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran upstream tests, spec cases, full pytest, root smoke, import checks, and official evaluation recorded 70 passed with solution_passed true.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial converted verification failures into concrete fixes and reran to green, while parallel did not finish the repair loop after its known failed local verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the run window through swarm work, integration testing, and a late repair delegation; status records timeout and the server log records parent prompt abort.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 708 seconds without timeout and status records substantial remaining budget under agent_completed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was forced by timeout during an active repair; serial closed after verified completion rather than budget exhaustion.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is serial_only_pass: the parallel artifact was evaluated at 65/70 after a timeout, while the serial artifact was evaluated at 70/70 after normal completion. The observable process difference is that parallel found unresolved integrated failures, delegated the necessary upstream-alignment repair to an active child, and then had that child and the parent prompt cancelled before the repair result was finalized. Serial performed the same kind of upstream/source/test alignment within one control trajectory, iterated through README/spec/full test failures, and ended with passing verification before completion.
parallel_contributors: After initial child work, the parent saw `7 failed, 18 passed` in root test.py, proving the assembled implementation still needed correction.
The parent delegated alignment with real v2.2.0 behavior to agent-6, but that repair child remained in progress and was stopped before finishing.
The official parallel status records a timeout and failed completed evaluation at 65/70.
serial_contributors: The serial main agent copied upstream v2.2.0 source and tests directly into /workspace.
It ran upstream tests, spec tests, and final full pytest/import checks until they passed.
It completed normally and the official evaluation recorded 70/70.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The first parallel assembly had ordinary implementation/test expectation mismatches in complex object handling, transformed_names behavior, and gen_features tests before the repair attempt.
Serial avoided much of that drift by copying upstream sources/tests early and patching only observed environment-specific doctest issues.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was explicitly assigned across child agents and then to a repair agent; the failure was not absence of an implementer.
The parent owned integration by inspecting the workspace, running imports and pytest, and delegating repair after failures; integration was not unowned.
Required files existed in the artifact and the parent checked the assembled tree; no missing final-package owner is shown.
The parent owned the end-to-end verification pipeline after children returned; the problem was the interrupted repair lifecycle, not absent pipeline ownership.
Parallel performed productive implementation immediately through the swarm; no mandatory serial preflight blocked implementation capacity.
The parallel run delegated implementation files directly rather than completing only an investigation phase before starting productive work.
The repair was delayed and cancelled, but the directly evidenced boundary is explicit early termination of an active repair child, not capacity being assigned away from the critical path.
The run used many agents and timed out, but the retained episode is the cancelled repair child; no separate fan-out episode has distinct anchors, consequence, and corrective action.
Agent-6 had a broad repair scope, but its unfinished state is explained by explicit cancellation before edits rather than proof the task was intrinsically too large for its window.
The child prompts included detailed file requirements, environment facts, and verification constraints; no known task requirement is proven absent from a child brief and followed to failure.
The components were assigned by file with explicit imports and expected APIs, and no concrete incompatibility is tied to an omitted inter-agent contract rather than ordinary implementation drift.
The repair prompt preserved the known failing tests and required reference-alignment facts; no known fact is shown disappearing in transfer.
The repair context was substantial but agent-6 reduced it into a concrete todo plan; the adverse event was interruption, not inability to consume an oversized handoff.
No receiver acted on superseded workspace or requirement information; the repair child was working from the current failing workspace state.
The record shows failing tests and reference comparisons, not incompatible returned handoffs that remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
The parallel parent did not make an observable whole-task completion claim; its prompt ended cancelled after visible failed tests and a failed repair child.
The repair child received explicit failed-test details, reference-source locations, and a concrete action list; it was not a retry without inherited checkpoint state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: After integrated pytest failed, the parent launched agent-6 for reference alignment and repair. Agent-6 had pending rewrite and verification tasks, then the session explicitly interrupted the active child and returned a failed child result stating it was stopped before finishing.
candidates.realized_consequence: The needed alignment repair was not finalized or joined, leaving the known failing local checks unresolved and the official parallel artifact failing 65/70.
candidates.near_match_reason: No Failure Takeover describes a downstream symptom of the same cancellation chain; the sharper observed boundary is the active repair child being interrupted before producing a result.

candidates.reason: No complete promotable repair candidate existed; agent-6 had only planned and pending work when it was interrupted.
There was no completed repair change merged after the relevant verification; the needed repair work never reached a merge point.
The initial child implementations were returned and present in the shared workspace, while the later repair implementation was not completed or retrievable before cancellation.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; the parent itself observed the failed pytest output.

The parent had already started a repair takeover by launching agent-6; after agent-6 was cancelled the parent turn was cancelled immediately, so there is no distinct takeover decision separate from Early Child Termination.
No completed child result with needed corrective content was available and ignored; the repair child never completed.
The parent actively inspected the workspace, imports, pytest failures, diffs, and then delegated repair; it did not merely wait without inspecting available progress.
Separate children wrote related files, but the record does not prove competing cross-file implementations caused an unreconciled design collision.
No two live agents are shown editing the same file and observing or reconciling a concurrent same-file change.
No non-entry source file is directly shown being wholesale replaced or deleted over another active owner's work.
The root test.py and package files were written by assigned owners; no required executable or submitted artifact overwrite by another live owner is proven.
There is no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing multiple current outputs and invalidating final-tree provenance.
Agents shared /workspace, but file ownership was explicit and no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem is shown beyond the interrupted repair.
No generated cache, fixture, temporary file, process, or auxiliary implementation from one actor is shown contaminating another actor's reference environment.

retained_patterns.reason: The parent had a known failing integrated workspace, delegated the necessary repair to agent-6, and that active repair child was explicitly interrupted before producing a finalized result. retained_patterns.near_match_reason: A takeover did not occur after cancellation, but that is not a separate episode because the parent itself was cancelled immediately; the primary event is early termination of the active child.
